newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Rate cut may follow good Portugal inflation news.
newsitem.headline: Rate cut may follow good Portugal inflation news.

text.p: Better-than-expected inflation figures for March open the way for Bank of Portugal to ease monetary policy on Friday when it sets conditions for the next commercial bank reserve period, analysts said.
The steadiness of the escudo against the mark and renewed optimism that monetary union will be launched on time should also encourage the cautious central bank to lower rates, they added.
"The room for manoeuvre of the Bank of Portugal...has risen (with the March inflation)," said analyst Pedro Braz Teixeira of Banco Santander de Negocios Portugal.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) announced on Tuesday that prices rose 0.1 percent month-on-month in March with the year-on-year rate slowing to 2.5 percent from 2.9 percent in February.
Analyst Martim Amaral Neto of Banco Essi said that the Bank should lower its repurchase pact rate by between 25 and 30 basis points to 6.20-6.25 percent.
"It makes no sense that Portugal's repo rate is 75 basis points (bp) above that of Spain," he said.
Spain's consumer price index for March will be released on Friday with analysts forecasting a year-on-year rate of 2.4 percent, down from 2.5 percent in February.
Portugal's inflation figure was better than the 2.6-2.7 percent year-on-year rate that analysts had forecast with the explanation lying in falling food prices.
"Food was a slight surprise. Prices fell, apparently across the board. This was the big factor," said Braz Teixeira.
Several analysts said the year-on-year rate could fall below two percent in April when meat price rises last year, triggered by the scare over mad cow disease, drop out of the index.
Isabel Costa of Banco Finantia said that the Bank of Portugal could respond to the inflation news with rate cuts of 20 basis points.
Analysts noted that the forward rate agreement (FRA) market was already anticipating that the repo rate would have been cut to around 5.75-5.80 percent by June.
